item.text: {"question_id":"3B.8","answer":"No. Although the constitutional framework formally recognized peaceful assembly, political parties, civil associations, and media freedoms, these were conditional on legal notification and are not evidence of effective protection in practice (BATCH-0024-R01-E009). In 2023, authorities routinely restricted assembly: more than 2,000 people were arrested for peaceful expression or assembly before mid-September, and more than 100 were reportedly arrested in October protests (BATCH-0002-E007; BATCH-0002-E013). The legal and administrative regime enabled prohibition, dispersal, force, website blocking, surveillance, and prosecution under broad security provisions; police reportedly rarely issued permits and authorities used force even against small peaceful groups (BATCH-0002-E013; BATCH-0002-E007). Organization and dissent were also obstructed through at least 140 documented arrests of Ahmed al-Tantawy campaign members and friends, arrests over critical social-media activity, reduced notary access from 389 offices in 2018 to 217 in 2023, physical assaults and police non-intervention at endorsement offices, and ineffective complaint handling (BATCH-0009-R03-E003; BATCH-0009-R03-E004; BATCH-0009-R03-E009). Security forces arrested and detained teachers protesting in October, while army and security forces used gunfire, beatings, vehicle impact, and detention against North Sinai residents protesting their right to return; Palestinian-solidarity demonstrators were also arrested after the president publicly called for demonstrations supporting the Palestinian cause (BATCH-0009-R03-E015). Surveillance of opposition candidate Ahmed Tantawi’s phone was attributed to the Egyptian government with high confidence on technical grounds, though not by a final judicial finding (BATCH-0002-E040). Accountability and remedy were weak: authorities made no arrests after reported attacks at the Engineers’ Syndicate, did not effectively investigate endorsement complaints, and continued prosecutions and detention; releases and presidential pardons occurred, including Patrick Zaki’s pardon and Mohamed el-Baqer’s release, but did not demonstrate structural correction (BATCH-0002-E013; BATCH-0009-R03-E003; BATCH-0009-R03-E010; BATCH-0009-R02-E016). Sisi’s National Dialogue commitments to inclusiveness and democratic practice were favorable rhetoric and a formal program, but the supplied evidence does not establish implementation and AFTE reports continuing repression during the process (BATCH-0019-E005; BATCH-0019-E006; BATCH-0009-R03-E003). The evidence therefore supports a recurring, sometimes widespread pattern of state retaliation and inadequate protection for peaceful protest, dissent, and organization, while not proving that Sisi personally ordered every local assault, arrest, or operational use of force.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0002-E040","BATCH-0009-R03-E003","BATCH-0009-R03-E004","BATCH-0009-R03-E009","BATCH-0009-R03-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-R01-E009","BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0019-E006","BATCH-0009-R03-E010","BATCH-0009-R02-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not provide a complete denominator for protests, arrests, uses of force, or permits.","Personal orders by Sisi are not established for each incident; attribution is principally to government, security, judicial, or army institutions under his government.","The Tantawi spyware attribution is a high-confidence technical assessment, not a final judicial finding.","The evidence documents releases and pardons but does not establish consistent independent investigation, accountability, compensation, or broader institutional remedy.","Some protest and assault accounts rely on AFTE documentation, testimonies, and human-rights reporting, and the NEA disputed some complaints."],"corrections_made":["Added the specific 2023 evidence on reduced notary access, at least 140 campaign-related arrests, police non-intervention and ineffective complaints, and North Sinai gunfire and detention.","Reweighted constitutional guarantees and National Dialogue statements as formal or rhetorical commitments without demonstrated implementation.","Corrected the treatment of October arrests to avoid implying that the supplied State Department passage specifically established violent dispersal in those cases.","Preserved releases and pardons as limited contrary evidence without treating them as systemic remedy.","Qualified ruler attribution and spyware attribution in accordance with the supplied evidence limitations."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
